page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine provisioned on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core and 2 threads on an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for instruction extensions such as AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES. Hardware resources include 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, paired with 100 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark metrics reflect strong single-core execution alongside typical scaling constraints inherent to a 2-vCPU configuration. The instance reaches the top tier in stress-ng single-core processing with a score of 3432.48, supported by top-quartile results in Geekbench single-core performance (2130.0) and single-threaded data compression tasks (32.12 GB/sec in gzip compression). Uncached memory bandwidth hovers in the median range with 76.08 GB/sec read and 74.06 GB/sec write speeds. Conversely, parallel execution throughput is bounded by the single physical core layout, resulting in lower-quartile scores across multi-core Geekbench (3815.0), PassMark CPU execution (5975.81), Clang compilation, and Redis set operations.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, this configuration trades aggregate parallel throughput for dedicated per-core responsiveness and generous memory allocation. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers a cost-effective operational profile for footprints requiring persistent in-memory datasets without incurring the billing overhead of larger multi-core instances. However, workloads requiring sustained concurrent I/O or multi-threaded CPU saturation will encounter bottlenecks on this platform.

Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is optimal for memory-bound applications with modest concurrency requirements, such as intermediate caching layers, lightweight relational databases, background queue workers, and single-stream data extraction pipelines.
description: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is a memory-oriented virtual server running on the AMD EPYC architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core running at 2.0 GHz, 16.0 GB of system RAM, and 100 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instructions. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and strong single-threaded compression throughput. However, overall multi-core throughput and network-intensive web serving are bounded by the low physical core count. The generous 8:1 memory-to-core ratio allows cost-efficient deployment of RAM-heavy services without purchasing unnecessary processing cores. This server type is best suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, small relational databases, text processing pipelines, and isolated background tasks.
